claims.text: The starting material is a near-equiatomic multi-principal-element automotive alloy catalyst.
A closed-loop high-throughput workflow can identify a modified catalyst with improved low-temperature activity, poisoning resistance, and lifetime durability.
The improved catalyst can be identified without increasing platinum-group-metal content.
The optimization workflow combines automated solvothermal synthesis, accelerated aging, activity screening, machine learning, and Bayesian optimization.
Iterative compositional tuning will produce optimized elemental distributions and microstructural features.
Potential optimized microstructures include a more uniform solid solution or controlled nanoscale phase segregation.
The optimized elemental distributions and microstructure will enhance active sites for CO and hydrocarbon oxidation.
The optimized elemental distributions and microstructure will mitigate poisoning and sintering.
Subtle compositional adjustments will fine-tune the local electronic and structural environment of the catalyst.
Fine-tuning the local electronic and structural environment will improve binding energies at active sites.
Improved active-site binding energies will lower catalyst light-off temperatures.
Improved active-site binding energies will increase resistance to poison-induced deactivation and long-term structural degradation.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the optimized catalyst will have lower light-off temperatures for CO and hydrocarbon oxidation.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the optimized catalyst will have greater resistance to H2O and NO poisoning.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the optimized catalyst will retain performance better during accelerated lifetime aging without higher platinum-group-metal loading.
The predicted improvements apply to simulated transient and low-temperature exhaust, including temperatures below 150 °C and exposure to H2O and NO.
Accelerated aging protocols can mimic full vehicle-lifetime degradation sufficiently to evaluate the durability prediction.
The laboratory result may not transfer if the simulated conditions omit real-world degradation mechanisms.
